title: Alt Text for Paper Figures
read: good. fig 5 is a line chart of stalled-state prevalence over the 50 min lab session, peaks at ~20 min and ~40 min (when the 2 harder tasks start)

**Figure 5 alt text (≈280 characters):**

> Line chart of the share of students in the stalled state over a 50-minute lab session. Stalling rises sharply and peaks around minute 20 and again around minute 40, the points at which the two harder tasks begin, and is lower between and after those peaks.

If you report the actual peak percentages in the text, you can add them in parentheses (e.g., "peaks near 20 minutes (31%)") — reviewers and screen-reader users both appreciate concrete numbers.
fig 4: bar chart, cohen's kappa per state across 3 raters. productive 0.78, stalled 0.66, help seeking 0.74, overall 0.71

**Figure 4 alt text (≈290 characters):**

> Bar chart of inter-rater agreement (Cohen's kappa) across three raters for each behavioral state. Productive work has the highest agreement at 0.78, followed by help-seeking at 0.74 and stalled at 0.66. Overall agreement across all states is 0.71.

Ordering the states by value in the alt text (rather than by the chart's left-to-right order) makes the main takeaway — *stalled is hardest to label* — easier to hear.

need alt text for figures in my uist camera ready (acm requires it). fig 1: system overview, TutorTrace replays a student's IDE session with a timeline at the bottom, colored segments for states (productive, stalled, help-seeking), side panel with the AI tutor chat. write it, under 400 chars

**Figure 1 alt text (≈330 characters):**

> Screenshot of the TutorTrace interface. The main area replays a student's code editor session. Along the bottom, a timeline shows colored segments for behavioral states: productive work, stalled, and help-seeking. A side panel on the right displays the student's conversation with the AI tutor, aligned to the timeline position.

Tips for ACM alt text:
* Describe **what the figure conveys**, not every pixel.
* Don't start with "Image of" — screen readers already announce it's an image.
* Put detailed data in the caption or text; alt text should stand alone but stay short.
